title: CD Platformer that goes with my music project, Cowboy Clean
author: nunu395
selftext:
I've been working on something like this for awhile now, to combine my music with a game.  I initially had a side scroller, but figured I'd try to take it a step further and make it into something 3D.  It is a work in progress, but it's fun for me and that was my ultimate goal haha.  Hopefully it's fun for others too!  If I can polish it up in a way that feels acceptable, I'll spread it around more.  The goal is to have a fun game that has some "prizes" to win, downloadable songs, merch if you hit certain scores, etc.  A fun way to interact with people listening to the music.

[https://cowboyclean.com/cleaningup3d.html](https://cowboyclean.com/cleaningup3d.html)

Hope you like it, and if you have any suggestions/fixes/improvements please let me know!

Thanks!

Matt - Cowboy Clean

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/nunu395 could you add more about how AI fit into your development process? Just mentioning that AI was used doesn't cut it. Under Rule 4, promotional posts need to contribute something by discussing how the game was actually made. Otherwise the sub gets buried in ads. If there's no update, this post may be removed.

replies.author: nunu395
replies.body: Sure thing.  I first used gemini studio to create a sidescrolling platformer (Pro). It got me pretty far, creating basic assets, SFX.  I used my songs and other collage work as themes for levels, and went from there.  I recently tried Fable to pick up where I left off, and that's been the basis for the updated 3D venture.  I have extremely little coding background, C++ in HS, some java and flash in the past.  Nothing of note.  I created a master plan of levels, enemies, weapons, sounds with Fable, then offloaded most of the work to Opus.  The game is procedurally generated now.
